mainTopic: Who may perform מילה, and being healed or given haircuts by non-Jews
overview: The amud opens by finishing the גמרא's discussion of a ברייתא about whether a ארמאי or a כותי may circumcise a Jewish baby. One approach explains that רבי מאיר means only a recognized expert doctor. In the end, though, the גמרא reverses the names in the ברייתא, and it solves a clash between two statements of רבי יהודה by saying one of them belongs to רבי יהודה הנשיא. רב חסדא then gives the פסוקים behind רבי יהודה, who requires the right intention for מילה, and רבי יוסי, who does not. Next, רב and רבי יוחנן argue over which פסוק disqualifies a גוי from doing a מילה. After two suggested differences are knocked down by a משנה about vows, the גמרא concludes that they differ about a woman, and it defends this using the story of צפורה. A new משנה then deals with medical treatment and haircuts from non-Jews. The גמרא defines ריפוי ממון as treating one's animal and ריפוי נפשות as treating one's own body. מר עוקבא adds that simply taking a non-Jew's advice about medicine is allowed.

steps.title: רבי מאיר means an expert doctor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי מאיר allows a ארמאי to circumcise only when he is a well-known expert doctor. It supports this with a teaching of רבי יוחנן brought by רב דימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about an expert doctor. As when רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: if the doctor was a recognized expert to the public, it is permitted to be treated by him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: how could רבי מאיר let a ארמאי circumcise a Jewish baby, when we worry he might harm the child? The answer is that רבי מאיר is talking about a known expert doctor. This answer works only if we do not reverse the names in the ברייתא; step 4 goes back to reversing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A famous expert will not risk his reputation by hurting a patient, so the worry about harm falls away. רבי יוחנן's rule, that you may be treated by a doctor who is a public expert, shows that this kind of reasoning is accepted. רבי מאיר's ruling is narrowed to this specific case.

keyTerms.meaning: A recognized expert known to the public
When [so-and-so] came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: [We are dealing] with an expert physician,
as when Rav Dimi came,
[he said that] Rabbi Yochanan says:
If he was a recognized expert to the public, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a challenge on רבי מאיר raised before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to an expert doctor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seems to allow any ארמאי to circumcise, even though we worry he might harm the child
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר allows it only with a recognized expert doctor, who would not risk his reputation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being treated by a doctor who is a recognized public expert is permitted

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really allow a כותי to circumcise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the version where רבי יהודה allows a כותי to circumcise. Another ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה forbidding it, because the כותי does it for the sake of הר גרזים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that a כותי is fine for circumcising? But a ברייתא teaches: a Jew may circumcise a כותי, but a כותי may not circumcise a Jew, because he circumcises for the sake of הר גרזים. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of the ברייתא, where רבי יהודה says a כותי may circumcise. It asks how that fits with another ברייתא where רבי יהודה says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is a contradiction: רבי יהודה cannot both allow and forbid a כותי. In the second ברייתא, his reason is that the כותי's intention is for הר גרזים and not for ה׳. So the current version of the first ברייתא seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan, a member of a group whose Jewishness was in doubt
It is fine, it is acceptable

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כּוּתִי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold that a Kuti is fine [to circumcise]?
But isn't it taught:
A Jew may circumcise a Kuti,
but a Kuti may not circumcise a Jew,
because he circumcises for the sake of Mount Gerizim,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כּוּתִי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבי מאיר's half, the גמרא turns to challenge רבי יהודה's half of the same ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of the ברייתא in which רבי יהודה permits a כותי to circumcise
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: another ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה forbidding a כותי because he circumcises for the sake of הר גרזים

steps.title: רבי יוסי rejects רבי יהודה's reason
steps.stepSummary: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי argues that the Torah never requires מילה to be done with the right intention. So a כותי may keep circumcising with no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: Where do we find in the Torah that מילה must be done for its own sake? Rather, the כותי may go on circumcising until his soul leaves him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of the ברייתא the גמרא just quoted. רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי יהודה and says the כותי's intention does not matter for מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי attacks the reason behind רבי יהודה's rule: מילה does not need the right intention, so a wrong intention does not ruin it. This confirms that in this ברייתא, רבי יהודה is clearly the one who forbids a כותי. That makes the contradiction from the last step even sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: And where do we find? (a pushback meaning 'there is no such source')
For its own sake, with the proper intention
Until his soul leaves him, meaning for his whole life

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
And where do we find
[that] circumcision from the Torah [must be done] for its own sake?
Rather, he may go on circumcising
until his soul departs!
phrases.notes: A colorful way of saying there's no problem at all. Let him keep doing it his whole life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וְכִי הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא used in the challenge, giving רבי יוסי's reply to רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יהודה's reason for forbidding a כותי, within the quoted ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah does not require מילה to be done with proper intention, so a wrong intention is no reason to forbid it

steps.title: Reverse the names, and the other רבי יהודה is רבי יהודה הנשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to reversing the opinions in the first ברייתא, as it did earlier. It solves the earlier clash between two statements of רבי יהודה by saying one of them belongs to רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really reverse the opinions as we reversed them originally. And as for the difficulty of רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה, that statement is from רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the problem. It flips the names in the first ברייתא, so that רבי יהודה forbids a כותי, which matches the second ברייתא. It also explains that the other statement that had been attributed to רבי יהודה was said by a different רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא had reversed the names but dropped the idea because of a clash with another statement of רבי יהודה. Now it brings the reversal back and removes that clash: the clashing statement belongs to רבי יהודה הנשיא, not to the רבי יהודה of our ברייתא. So there is no contradiction, just two different תנאים with two different views.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (returning to an earlier approach)
Reverse (switch the names of who said what)

steps.whatToRemember: With the names reversed: רבי מאיר allows a כותי and forbids a ארמאי, and רבי יהודה allows a ארמאי and forbids a כותי, which matches the הר גרזים ברייתא. The statement that a גוי's מילה is invalid, which seemed to clash with רבי יהודה, was really said by רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people called רבי יהודה here. The plain 'רבי יהודה' of the ברייתא is not the same person as רבי יהודה הנשיא, so their statements cannot contradict each other.

phrases.english: Rather, actually reverse [the opinions]
as we reversed them originally,
phrases.notes: This points back to the previous amud, where the גמרא first switched the names in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and as for what was difficult,
[one statement] of Rabbi Yehuda against [another of] Rabbi Yehuda,
that one is [the opinion] of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from steps 2-3 by bringing back the earlier reversal and assigning the clashing statement to a different תנא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the names in the ברייתא and attributing the clashing statement to a different person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reversal seemed impossible because it made רבי יהודה contradict himself
steps.terutzMaskana: Reverse the names. The other statement is from רבי יהודה הנשיא, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה הנשיא disqualifies a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its claim from Step 4 by quoting a ברייתא where רבי יהודה הנשיא learns from a פסוק that מילה done by a גוי is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה הנשיא says, how do we know that a circumcision done by a non-Jew is not valid? The פסוק says: "And you shall keep My covenant."
steps.whatsHappening: In Step 4 the גמרא said one of the statements belongs to רבי יהודה הנשיא. Now it proves this: there really is a ברייתא where רבי יהודה הנשיא rules that a גוי cannot do a valid מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up the answer from Step 4 with a real source. רבי יהודה הנשיא reads "you shall keep My covenant" as limiting מילה to people who are themselves part of the covenant. So a גוי is disqualified.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
From where do we know that circumcision by a non-Jew
is not valid?
The verse teaches:
"And you shall keep My covenant."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the answer from Step 4 that one statement belongs to רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה הנשיא holds מילה by a גוי is not valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה הנשיא, based on בראשית 17:9.

steps.title: רב חסדא gives the פסוקים behind רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains which פסוק each side uses: רבי יהודה needs intention because of "to ה׳ shall be circumcised," and רבי יוסי does not because of "he must surely be circumcised."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is רבי יהודה's reason? Because it is written: "To ה׳ let him be circumcised." And רבי יוסי learns from: "He must surely be circumcised."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument from Steps 2-3 about whether מילה needs the right intention. רב חסדא tells us the source from the Torah for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads "to ה׳" as meaning the מילה must be done for ה׳'s sake, so a כותי, who does it for הר גרזים, is not allowed. רבי יוסי points to the doubled word "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל", which shows that מילה works no matter who does it or with what intention.

keyTerms.meaning: To ה׳ let him be circumcised
He must surely be circumcised (a doubled verb)

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי יהודה here is the one from the ברייתא in Step 2, who required intention for the sake of ה׳. He is not רבי יהודה הנשיא from Step 5.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: "To ה׳ let him be circumcised."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:48. "To ה׳" means the מילה has to be done for ה׳'s sake.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei learns from: "He must surely be circumcised."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:13. The verb is said twice, and רבי יוסי learns from that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from who may circumcise to the Torah sources for the argument about intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה learns intention from "לַה׳ הִמּוֹל"; רבי יוסי learns that no intention is needed from "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל".

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי deal with "to ה׳"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי יוסי: the Torah clearly says "to ה׳ let him be circumcised," so why not require intention?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יוסי: isn't it written "To ה׳ let him be circumcised"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי with רבי יהודה's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah says the מילה is "to ה׳," it seems to demand intention. רבי יוסי must explain what these words mean to him.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)

phrases.english: And the other one, isn't it written:
phrases.notes: "The other one" here is רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: "To ה׳ let him be circumcised"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי from רבי יהודה's פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that מילה needs no intention.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah says "to ה׳," which seems to require intention.

steps.title: "To ה׳" goes on the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that "to ה׳" belongs to the קרבן פסח mentioned in that פסוק, not to the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is written about the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי: the words "to ה׳" describe the פסח, not the מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a convert who wants to bring the פסח. רבי יוסי reads it as "bring the פסח to ה׳," so it says nothing about intention for מילה.

phrases.english: That is written about the Passover offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so the phrase belongs to a different subject.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "To ה׳" describes the מילה, so intention is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: "To ה׳" describes the פסח, so רבי יוסי does not need intention for מילה.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה deal with the doubled word?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks רבי יהודה: the Torah says "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל," so why not learn from it like רבי יוסי?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too, רבי יהודה: isn't it written "He must surely be circumcised"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns around and challenges רבי יהודה with רבי יוסי's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled verb seems to teach something extra: that מילה counts no matter how it is done. רבי יהודה must explain why he does not learn this.

phrases.english: And the other one too, isn't it written:
phrases.notes: This time "the other one" is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: "He must surely be circumcised"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 7, now attacking the other side.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that intention is required.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubled verb seems to teach that any מילה is valid.

steps.title: The Torah speaks the way people speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the doubled verb is just normal speech and teaches nothing extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה: repeating the verb is just how people talk, so we do not learn a new law from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי treats the double word as a hint to a new law. רבי יהודה holds that such doubling is simply the Torah's normal style. So "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל" does not cancel the need for intention.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah speaks the way people speak, so extra words are not always teaching something new

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: מילה needs intention ("לַה׳ הִמּוֹל"), and the doubled verb is just normal speech. רבי יוסי: no intention is needed ("הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל"), and "to ה׳" goes on the פסח.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יהודה and closes this back-and-forth.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Saying the extra wording is ordinary speech that teaches nothing new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled verb teaches that any מילה counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubling is just normal style, so intention is still required.

steps.title: רב and רבי יוחנן argue about the source for disqualifying a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: A new argument: רב learns from "you shall keep My covenant" that מילה by a גוי is not valid, and רבי יוחנן learns it from "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל."
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: How do we know that circumcision by a non-Jew is not valid? דרו בר פפא said in the name of רב: "And you shall keep My covenant." And רבי יוחנן said: "He must surely be circumcised."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between אמוראים. Both agree a גוי's מילה is not valid; they only argue about which פסוק teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב uses the same פסוק as רבי יהודה הנשיא in Step 5. רבי יוחנן uses "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל," reading it as: the one who is circumcised should do the circumcising.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רבי יוסי! He used "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל" to be lenient. רבי יוחנן uses the same words to disqualify a גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both views agree on the הלכה that a גוי's מילה is not valid; they only argue about the source.

phrases.english: It was stated: From where do we know that circumcision by a non-Jew
is not valid?

phrases.aramaic: דָּרוּ בַּר פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר:
phrases.english: Daru bar Pappa said in the name of Rav:
"And you shall keep My covenant."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק that רבי יהודה הנשיא used in Step 5.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan learns it from: "He must surely be circumcised."
phrases.notes: He reads it as: one who is circumcised should circumcise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: מִנַּיִן לְמִילָה בְּגוֹי שֶׁהִיא פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of Step 5 (a גוי doing מילה) with a new argument between אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה by a גוי is not valid. רב learns it from "וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר"; רבי יוחנן learns it from "הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל".

steps.title: What is the difference between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רב and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two sources from step 11 lead to any different result in practice. This short question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and רבי יוחנן agree that a גוי may not do a מילה. They only disagree about which פסוק teaches it. The גמרא wants to know if that disagreement ever changes the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (a request for a practical difference)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical difference comes out of the two derivations given in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two sources would give different rulings.

steps.title: First suggestion: a circumcised Arab
steps.stepSummary: The difference would be a circumcised Arab or גבנוני. Under 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' he may do a מילה. Under 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִּשְׁמֹר' he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A circumcised Arab or a circumcised גבנוני is the difference between them. The one who learns from 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' would say he may do a מילה. The one who learns from 'you shall keep My covenant' would say he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a case where the two sources disagree: a non-Jew who is himself circumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' as 'only one who is circumcised may circumcise', so a circumcised Arab would qualify. רב reads 'keep My covenant' as 'only one who is part of the covenant, a Jew', so a non-Jew is out even if he is circumcised.

keyTerms.meaning: A member of a non-Jewish people who also circumcised
There is (a reason to allow) / there is not

phrases.english: A circumcised Arab and a circumcised Gavnuni
is the difference between them.
The one who says 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל': there is (a reason to allow him),
and the one who says 'you shall keep My covenant': there is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַרְבִי מָהוּל וְגַבְנוּנִי מָהוּל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a proposed case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A circumcised non-Jew may do a מילה under 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' but not under 'אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִּשְׁמֹר'.

steps.title: Challenge: circumcised non-Jews still count as uncircumcised
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about vows shows that circumcised non-Jews are treated as uncircumcised. So even under 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' they would not qualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would the one who says 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' really allow it? We learned in a משנה: if someone says 'Benefit from the uncircumcised is קונם for me', he may benefit from uncircumcised Jews but not from circumcised non-Jews. So even when non-Jews are circumcised, they are treated as uncircumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion of step 13. It brings a משנה showing that a circumcised non-Jew is not considered 'circumcised' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the way people talk, 'the uncircumcised' means non-Jews and 'the circumcised' means Jews. So a circumcised Arab is still in the 'uncircumcised' group. That means even רבי יוחנן's 'only a circumcised person' rule would exclude him, and the difference falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a vow forbidding something on oneself

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, 'circumcised' and 'uncircumcised' are labels for Jews and non-Jews. They are not about the actual physical state of each person.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל', is there (a reason to allow him)?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: קוּנָּם שֶׁאֲנִי נֶהֱנֶה מִן הָעֲרֵלִים —
phrases.english: But we learned: 'Benefit from the uncircumcised is קונם (forbidden) for me',
he is permitted with uncircumcised Jews,
and forbidden with the circumcised of the nations of the world;
so we see that even though they are circumcised,
they are treated like those who are not circumcised!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proposed difference of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that under 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' a circumcised Arab may do a מילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vow משנה shows that circumcised non-Jews are halachically 'uncircumcised', so 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' also excludes them.

steps.title: Second suggestion: a Jew who could not be circumcised
steps.stepSummary: The difference is instead a Jew left uncircumcised because his brothers died from מילה. He qualifies under 'keep My covenant' but not under 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference is a Jew whose brothers died because of מילה, so they did not circumcise him. The one who learns from 'And you shall keep My covenant' would allow him to circumcise. The one who learns from 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' would not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the Arab case and offers a new difference: an uncircumcised Jew who was allowed to stay that way for safety.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This flips the earlier case. Now the person is Jewish but not physically circumcised. רב only requires being part of the covenant, so he may do a מילה. רבי יוחנן requires being circumcised, so he may not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier suggestion for a new one)
His brothers died because of מילה

phrases.english: Rather, the difference between them is
a Jew whose brothers died because of מילה,
and they did not circumcise him.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר״ — אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: According to the one who says 'And you shall keep My covenant': there is (a reason to allow him),
according to the one who says 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל': there is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case that step 14 knocked down with a new proposed difference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was a circumcised non-Jew.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is an uncircumcised Jew whose brothers died from מילה.

steps.title: Challenge: uncircumcised Jews still count as circumcised
steps.stepSummary: The same vow משנה shows that uncircumcised Jews are treated as circumcised. So under 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' too, such a Jew should qualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would the one who says 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' really not allow it? We learned: if someone says 'Benefit from the circumcised is קונם for me', he is forbidden even with uncircumcised Jews and permitted with circumcised non-Jews. So even when Jews are not circumcised, they are treated as circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new suggestion using the other half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every Jew counts as 'circumcised', then even רבי יוחנן's rule would allow this Jew to do a מילה. That means the second suggested difference also seems to disappear.
steps.whatToRemember: The vow משנה treats 'circumcised' as meaning Jews and 'uncircumcised' as meaning non-Jews. This has now knocked down both suggested differences between רב and רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל', is there really no (reason to allow him)?
But we learned: 'Benefit from the circumcised is קונם for me',
he is forbidden with uncircumcised Jews
and permitted with the circumcised of the nations of the world,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְהִילִי
phrases.english: so we see that even though they are not circumcised,
they are treated like those who are circumcised!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second proposed difference of step 15, using the same משנה as step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that under 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' an uncircumcised Jew may not do a מילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vow משנה shows that uncircumcised Jews are halachically 'circumcised', so 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' would include them.

steps.title: The real difference is a woman
steps.stepSummary: After the last answer was knocked down, the גמרא offers a new practical difference: a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is a woman. According to the one who learns from 'And you shall keep My covenant,' she may not perform מילה, because a woman is not part of the מילה obligation. According to the one who learns from 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל,' she may, because a woman is treated like someone who is already circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the uncircumcised-Jew case, which step 16 knocked down. It suggests a woman is where the two sources give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'keep My covenant' only includes people who are part of the covenant of מילה, and a woman is not. The verse 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' is read as 'one who is circumcised may circumcise.' A woman counts as naturally circumcised, so she qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is part of the מילה obligation
She is considered like one who is circumcised
There is not / there is (here: she does not qualify / she does qualify)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: the two sources disagree about a woman. 'Keep My covenant' rules her out. 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' allows her.

phrases.english: Rather, the difference between them is a woman.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמוֹר״ — לֵיכָּא,
phrases.english: According to the one who says 'And you shall keep My covenant,' she may not.
since a woman is not part of the מילה obligation.
And according to the one who says 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל,' she may,
since a woman is considered like one who is circumcised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case from step 15 with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitutes a new case for the practical difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was an uncircumcised Jew whose brothers died from מילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is a woman. The two verses give opposite results for her.

steps.title: צפורה circumcised her son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that a woman may not perform מילה, using the story of צפורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really anyone who says a woman may not? But it is written: 'And צפורה took a flint'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the opinion that rules out a woman. It points to a פסוק where a woman clearly did a מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה describes צפורה circumcising her son, it seems hard for any opinion to say a woman is not allowed. So the 'keep My covenant' side looks contradicted by a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really anyone who says...?

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אִשָּׁה לָא?
phrases.english: And is there really anyone who says a woman may not?
But it is written: 'And צפורה took a flint'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אִשָּׁה לָא? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one side of the difference proposed in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that a woman may not perform מילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows a woman doing a מילה, so the opinion seems to contradict the תורה.

steps.title: Read it as 'she had someone take'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the word with different vowels: צפורה had someone else take the flint.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as 'וַתַּקַּח': she caused the flint to be taken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'no woman' opinion. It reads the word as if צפורה had someone else take the flint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the vowels changes 'she took' into 'she caused to be taken.' So the פסוק no longer proves she did the act herself.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as (with a different vowel reading)
And she caused to be taken

phrases.english: Read it as 'וַתַּקַּח': she caused it to be taken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק with different vowels
steps.terutzMaskana: She had someone else take it.

steps.title: But the פסוק says she cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the same פסוק says 'and she cut off.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And she cut off'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading again. Even if someone else took the flint, the פסוק says צפורה did the cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking a flint is only preparation. Cutting is the מילה itself, and the פסוק seems to say she cut.

phrases.english: But it is written: 'And she cut off'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19 from the next word in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that צפורה only had others act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'she cut off' describes the act of מילה itself as done by her.

steps.title: She told someone else to cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads this word too as causative: צפורה told another man to cut, and he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as 'וַתַּכְרֵת': she caused it to be cut, since she told another person and he did it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same method again. It reads 'she cut' as 'she had it cut,' meaning another man did the מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words in the פסוק now mean צפורה gave instructions while a man did the actual work. So the פסוק does not prove a woman may perform מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And she caused to be cut off

phrases.english: Read it as 'וַתַּכְרֵת': she caused it to be cut off,
since she told another person and he did it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 with the same vowel-reading method.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק with different vowels
steps.terutzMaskana: Another man cut at her instruction.

steps.title: She started and משה finished
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: צפורה began the מילה, and משה came and completed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: she came and began, and משה came and finished it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way out that keeps the plain reading of the פסוק. צפורה started, but משה finished the מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here צפורה really did cut, but the מילה was completed by a man who is obligated in מילה. So the פסוק still does not prove a woman can perform a full מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you want, say instead:
she came and began it,
phrases.notes: The round-bracket word is in the printed גמרא; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. Both mean 'she came.'

phrases.english: and משה came and finished it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the צפורה challenge without changing the vowels.
steps.terutzMaskana: She only started it. משה completed it.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'no woman' opinion survives. Either צפורה had a man do the מילה, or she began and משה finished.

steps.title: משנה: healing and haircuts from non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules on being treated medically by non-Jews and getting a haircut from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may be healed by them with 'monetary healing,' but not with 'healing of lives.' One may not get a haircut from them anywhere, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: in a public place it is allowed, but not when the two are alone.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows one kind of medical care from a non-Jew and forbids another. It also brings a מחלוקת about haircuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that a non-Jew might harm the Jew, so some situations are allowed and some are not. רבי מאיר forbids haircuts everywhere. The חכמים allow them in public, where others are watching.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Monetary healing' (meaning is explained in the גמרא)
'Healing of lives' (meaning is explained in the גמרא)
Privately, just the two of them

phrases.english: משנה: One may be healed by them with 'monetary healing,'
but not with 'healing of lives.'
And one may not get a haircut from them anywhere,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the חכמים say: in a public area it is allowed,
but not when the two are alone together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Monetary healing' from a non-Jew is allowed, 'healing of lives' is not. Haircuts are forbidden everywhere according to רבי מאיר. The חכמים allow them only in public.

steps.title: What do the two kinds of healing mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'ריפוי ממון' and 'ריפוי נפשות' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'monetary healing,' and what is 'healing of lives'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking what the משנה's two unclear terms mean. This sets up the attempts to define them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words are not self-explanatory. Before discussing the rule, the גמרא needs to know what exactly is allowed and what is forbidden.

phrases.english: גמרא: What is 'monetary healing,'
and what is 'healing of lives'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of terms in the משנה of step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of 'ריפוי ממון' and 'ריפוי נפשות'.

steps.title: Paid versus free healing is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the terms mean paid versus free treatment, then rejects this because the משנה would have said so plainly.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'monetary healing' means for pay and 'healing of lives' means for free, then the משנה should have said: one may be healed by them for pay, but not for free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first definition and immediately pushes back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the difference were only about payment, the משנה would have used the simple words 'for pay' and 'for free.' Since it chose different words, they must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Let it teach (the משנה should have said)

phrases.english: If you say 'monetary healing' means for pay,
and 'healing of lives' means for free,
then let it teach: one may be healed by them for pay,
but not for free!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 24 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the terms mean paid versus free healing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה would have used the plain words 'for pay' and 'for free' if that were the meaning.

steps.title: A new suggestion: danger versus no danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that ריפוי ממון means treating a condition with no danger, and ריפוי נפשות means treating a condition that is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, "monetary treatment" means treating something that is not dangerous, and "personal treatment" means treating something that is dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The paid-versus-free idea was just rejected, so the גמרא offers a second way to read the משנה's two terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the משנה would allow a non-Jew to treat minor problems but not life-threatening ones. The line between the two cases becomes how serious the illness is.

keyTerms.meaning: "Monetary treatment." The kind of treatment the משנה allows.
"Personal treatment." The kind of treatment the משנה forbids.

phrases.english: Rather, "monetary treatment" —
means a matter that has no danger,
"personal treatment" —
means a matter that has danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, ״רִיפּוּי מָמוֹן״ — דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ סַכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected paid-versus-free reading from step 25 with a new definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of ריפוי ממון and ריפוי נפשות.

steps.title: Even a small bloodletting cut may not be treated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the danger-based reading from רב יהודה, who forbids being treated by non-Jews even for the minor cut left after bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say: Even for the cut of a bloodletting, we may not be treated by them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion it just made by quoting רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bloodletting cut is not dangerous, so the last suggestion would allow a non-Jew to treat it. רב יהודה forbids this, so the line cannot be drawn by how dangerous the condition is.

keyTerms.meaning: The cut made by a bloodletting tool. A minor wound.
"But didn't he say?" A formula that opens a challenge.

phrases.english: But didn't רב יהודה say:
Even the cut of a bloodletting
we may not be treated by them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the definition proposed in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that ריפוי ממון means a condition with no danger.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה forbids treatment even for a harmless bloodletting cut, so non-dangerous treatment cannot be what the משנה allows.

steps.title: Final answer: the animal versus one's own body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that ריפוי ממון means treating one's animal and ריפוי נפשות means treating one's own body, which fits רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, "monetary treatment" means treating his animal, and "personal treatment" means treating his own body. That is why רב יהודה said: Even for the cut of a bloodletting, we may not be treated by them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final definition of the two terms and shows that it agrees with רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal is the person's property (ממון), so a non-Jew may treat it. Any treatment of the person's own body is ריפוי נפשות and is forbidden, however minor. That explains why רב יהודה forbids even treating a bloodletting cut.

keyTerms.meaning: "And this is what he said." Shows that an earlier statement fits the new explanation.

steps.whatToRemember: ריפוי ממון means treating one's animal, and that is allowed. ריפוי נפשות means treating one's own body, and that is forbidden even for something as minor as a bloodletting cut.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the attempts. Paid versus free and danger versus no danger were both rejected. The final answer is the animal versus one's own body.

phrases.english: Rather, "monetary treatment" means his animal,
"personal treatment" means his own body,
and this is what רב יהודה said:
Even the cut of a bloodletting
we may not be treated by them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new definition that avoids the challenge in step 27 and quotes רב יהודה as support.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A Jew may have a non-Jew treat his animal but not his own body, not even for a minor wound.

steps.title: Taking a non-Jew's advice about medicine is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא in the name of מר עוקבא rules that if a non-Jew only says a certain medicine is good or bad for the condition, it is permitted to follow that advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: But if he told him, "Such-and-such a medicine is good for it" or "such-and-such a medicine is bad for it," it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement limits the ban: the problem is the non-Jew treating the person, not simply giving advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being treated by a non-Jew on one's body was just forbidden. רב חסדא adds that hearing which medicine helps or harms is a different case, and it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Good for it, meaning helpful for the illness.
Bad for it, meaning harmful for the illness.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows exactly where the ban stops: being treated is forbidden, but receiving information is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: רב חסדא said that מר עוקבא said:
But if he said to him:
phrases.notes: The non-Jew is speaking to the Jew who is sick.

phrases.english: "Such-and-such a medicine is good for it,"
"such-and-such a medicine is bad for it" —
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ban on bodily treatment from step 28 by allowing advice alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may follow a non-Jew's advice that a certain medicine is good or bad for an illness.
